Topics · Prayer and closeness to God

Why do even non-believers pray in emergencies?

When every means fails, many are left with one call. What is that call? The answer comes from your own memory.

Part 1 of 3

﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُسَيِّرُكُمْ فِى ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ وَفَرِحُوا۟ بِهَا جَآءَتْهَا رِيحٌ عَاصِفٌ وَجَآءَهُمُ ٱلْمَوْجُ مِن كُلِّ مَكَانٍ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ ۙ دَعَوُا۟ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ لَئِنْ أَنجَيْتَنَا مِنْ هَـٰذِهِۦ لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلشَّـٰكِرِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them[518] by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes a storm wind and the waves come upon them from every place and they expect to be engulfed, they supplicate Allāh, sincere to Him in religion, "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."

Translator's notes

[518] The change in pronoun from the second to third person shows that the following description applies specifically to the disbelievers.

Quran · Yunus 10:22

Translation

Out of my distress, I called on Yah. Yah answered me with freedom.

Original · Hebrew

מִֽן־הַ֭מֵּצַ֥ר קָרָ֣אתִי יָּ֑הּ עָנָ֖נִי בַמֶּרְחָ֣ב יָֽהּ׃

the Psalms · 118:5

World English Bible

The verse paints a scene any sailor knows: a fair wind and joy, then waves from every side, and the sense of being surrounded. At that point the call changes: people turn to God alone, sincerely. Notice what has fallen away: sect, group, argument, habit. If something remains when all of that is gone, perhaps it was never acquired. That proves nothing for everyone, but it deserves the question.

A question for you

In the worst hour you have known, what happened inside you?

If you sayI called out to someone I could not see
ThenThat is what the verse describes. It is left to you to ask who you thought was listening.
If you sayI called no one
ThenThat is honest, and it is no failing. Not everyone calls out in danger; the verse describes a tendency, not a law. You might ask whether that silence was calm or tired.
If you sayI don't think it means anything
ThenA view worth hearing: fear produces many things. The next part asks about what happens after the fear has passed.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ ٱلضُّرُّ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ ضَلَّ مَن تَدْعُونَ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ ۖ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰكُمْ إِلَى ٱلْبَرِّ أَعْرَضْتُمْ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ كَفُورًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when adversity touches you at sea, lost are [all] those you invoke except for Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away [from Him]. And ever is man ungrateful.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:67

Translation

Then they cry to Yahweh in their trouble, and he brings them out of their distress. He makes the storm a calm, so that its waves are still. Then they are glad because it is calm, so he brings them to their desired haven.

Original · Hebrew

וַיִּצְעֲק֣וּ אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם וּֽ֝מִמְּצֽוּקֹתֵיהֶ֗ם יוֹצִיאֵֽם׃ יָקֵ֣ם סְ֭עָרָה לִדְמָמָ֑ה וַ֝יֶּחֱשׁ֗וּ גַּלֵּיהֶֽם׃ וַיִּשְׂמְח֥וּ כִֽי־יִשְׁתֹּ֑קוּ וַ֝יַּנְחֵ֗ם אֶל־מְח֥וֹז חֶפְצָֽם׃

the Psalms · 107:28-30

World English Bible

﴿فَلَمَّآ أَنجَىٰهُمْ إِذَا هُمْ يَبْغُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ ۗ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّمَا بَغْيُكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُم ۖ مَّتَـٰعَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۖ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَنُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

But when He saves them, at once they commit injustice[519] upon the earth without right. O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves, [being merely] the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.

Translator's notes

[519] By oppression and disobedience or by invoking others besides Allāh.

Quran · Yunus 10:23

A sceptic says: that was only fear, so of course it ends when the fear ends. The verses describe the same pattern and ask something else: those you called on vanish, and once rescued you turn away. In danger you saw how little you control, and that was accurate. So the question turns round. Not why we call when afraid, but why we forget when safe. The second verse names what follows rescue, a word the Quran also uses for why people divided.

A question for you

Why do we forget in safety what we knew in danger?

If you sayComfort makes us forget
ThenThat is close to what the verse says of ease. It suggests forgetting here is not ignorance but distraction.
If you sayBecause what we knew was an illusion
ThenA possibility worth keeping in view. Notice, though, that you are comparing two states and ruling the safe one more truthful. What tips that for you?
If you sayI have not forgotten
ThenThat is a gift. Your question may be what has changed in your days because of what you remember.

Part 3 of 3

﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا ۚ فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا ۚ لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

So direct your face [i.e., self] toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fiṭrah[1145] of Allāh upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allāh.[1146] That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.

Translator's notes

[1145] The natural inborn inclination of man to worship his Creator prior to the corruption of his nature by external influences. Thus, Islāmic monotheism is described as the religion of fiṭrah - that of the inherent nature of mankind. [1146] i.e., let people remain true to their fiṭrah within the religion of Islām.

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:30

Translation

(for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves, in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)

Original · Ancient Greek

ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος· οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,

Romans · 2:14-15

World English Bible

The verse proposes an explanation: there is in people a first nature that leans toward its Maker and is not erased, though habit may cover it. If so, the names and groups that divide people were all laid over something shared, a unity older than any of them. This is no proof that binds anyone; a psychological account is a real rival. But it would explain why people who differ know the same call when all that divides them falls away.

A question for you

Which account comes nearest to what you know of yourself?

If you sayA nature in people
ThenThen for you people share something before all that divides them, and that opens the question of what happened next.
If you sayFear and inherited habit
ThenAn account with real weight. One question remains: does it cover those raised with none of it? The answer is yours to give.
If you sayI don't know yet
ThenNo hurry. This is one of those questions that grows along with the person asking.

The same in the other books

Translation

Then they cried to Yahweh in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses.

the Psalms · 107:6

World English Bible

Translation

Behold, I have only found this: that God made mankind upright; but they search for many inventions.”

Original · Hebrew

לְבַד֙ רְאֵה־זֶ֣ה מָצָ֔אתִי אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָאָדָ֖ם יָשָׁ֑ר וְהֵ֥מָּה בִקְשׁ֖וּ חִשְּׁבֹנ֥וֹת רַבִּֽים׃

Ecclesiastes · 7:29

World English Bible

The Master said, 'Man is born for uprightness. If a man lose his uprightness, and yet live, his escape from death is the effect of mere good fortune.'

Chinese classics · Analects 6.17

Confucian Analects (Legge)

Your reflection

If you could write one line to yourself on a safe day, from something you learned on a hard one, what would it say?
